column1: GitHub Actions workflow YAML files belong in the repository's {{c1::.github\workflows}} directory.
column2:
GitHub looks in this directory for workflow definitions. Commit the workflow beside the SQL project so changes to the build or deployment process can be reviewed with changes to the schema.
Review source

column1: A GitHub Actions deploy job waits for a successful job with ID build by setting {{c1::needs: build}}.
column2:
The value build is the upstream job ID. By default, the deploy job runs only after that job succeeds. Defining both jobs without a dependency does not enforce that order.
Review source

column1: Upload a built .dacpac for use in another GitHub Actions job with {{c1::actions/upload-artifact}}.
column2:
The upload action saves the exact package produced by the build. Name it so a later job can retrieve it even when the deploy job runs on a different runner.
Review source

column1: Retrieve a previously uploaded .dacpac in a GitHub deploy job with {{c1::actions/download-artifact}}.
column2:
The download action restores an artifact by name. Use the artifact that staging tested rather than compiling the same source again in the deploy job.
Review source

column1: To request an OIDC token, grant the GitHub job or workflow {{c1::id-token: write}} under permissions.
column2:
This permission lets GitHub issue an identity token for the workflow. It does not grant Azure permissions. Azure validates the token against a matching federated credential before granting access.
Review source

column1: Attach a GitHub deploy job to the production environment with {{c1::environment: production}}.
column2:
The job references the environment by name. Its configured approval and branch rules control when it starts, and its environment secrets are available only to jobs that reference that environment.
Review source

column1: To allow only main to deploy to a GitHub environment, configure its {{c1::deployment branches and tags}} rules.
column2:
Environment branch rules control which branches can deploy to that environment. A trigger filter only controls when a workflow starts, so it is not a substitute for the environment rule.
Review source

column1: In SqlAzureDacpacDeployment@1, the {{c1::azureSubscription}} input identifies the Azure service connection.
column2:
The service connection provides the Azure identity the task uses. The input expects that connection's name, not the subscription display name or a database password.
Review source

column1: Assign automatic GitHub review requests by file pattern in a {{c1::CODEOWNERS}} file.
column2:
A matching file pattern requests review from its named owner. For example, assign SQL files to a team with write access. Set a separate protection rule if you need to require the owner's approval.
Review source

column1: A GitHub Actions environment wait timer starts when the deployment job is {{c1::initially triggered}}, not after approval.
column2:
The timer starts when the job is first triggered. If approval takes longer than the timer, the timer does not restart. Do not treat it as a guaranteed delay after approval.
Review source

column1: For an Azure DevOps Branch control check, specify main as {{c1::refs/heads/main}}.
column2:
The check uses the full Git branch reference, not the short branch name. Use refs/heads/main so Azure DevOps can match main to the allowed-branch list.
Review source
